neighbours.label: first sub-word piece of a word split before a diminutive/frequentative ending (gig|gle, nib|ble, trem|ulous)
fire: Halfway through the lecture she began to giggle uncontrollably.
The rabbit would nibble at the clover by the fence.
After the storm the old shed began to wobble in the wind.
He could hear the children giggling behind the curtain.
The hamster nibbled on a sunflower seed in its cage.
Her hands were tremulous as she signed the contract.
The tiny fish began to nibble at our toes in the lake.
My little brother tried hard not to giggle during the sermon.
quiet: Halfway through the lecture she began to laugh uncontrollably.
The rabbit would chew at the clover by the fence.
After the storm the old shed began to shake in the wind.
He could hear the children laughing behind the curtain.
The hamster munched on a sunflower seed in its cage.
Her hands were shaking as she signed the contract.
The tiny fish began to bite at our toes in the lake.
My little brother tried hard not to smile during the sermon.

notes: Card: nib|ble, gig|gle, trem|ulous, NIB|IRU; output suppresses 'led/ling/le'. Probe: giggle 0.45, nibbles 0.67.
